_note: Ellington's own live page for the original Belgravia (Belgravia I, JVC, launched 2015, handed over 2017) is still up and carries its own media. All 9 images below come from that page's hero slider (2 slides), its three-up 'MainSection' widget (3) and its gallery widget (4); every asset path is literally Belgravia-I-*, so they belong to this building and not to a sibling. Every image was opened at full size and looked at before it was described. EXCLUDED: /wp-content/uploads/One-River-Point_Club-House-1.jpg (site-wide enquiry pop-up, a different Ellington project), summer-1.jpg (site-wide promo panel), Belgravia-Heights-I-Inner-600x400.jpg, bulgeria2-600x400.jpg and belgravia3-1-e1716891175817-600x400.jpg (the 'Explore similar properties' cards for Belgravia Heights I, Belgravia II and Belgravia III - explicitly out of scope), plus Ellington logos, footer logo, share/arrow/close SVGs and the Kenyt chatbot icons. No agency or portal source was used or opened. BROCHURE: gated - the page offers only 'ENQUIRE' and 'CONSTRUCTION UPDATE' buttons, both of which open a form demanding name, email and phone. No form was filled and no brochure was requested, so no brochure imagery is included. HONEST WEAKNESS: there is no true street-level elevation or aerial of Belgravia on the developer's page. The only wide exterior photography Ellington publishes here is shot from inside the central courtyard, so both exterior candidates are flagged as partial.

images.note: LOOKED: EXTERIOR, photograph, ground-level view taken from inside the building's own central courtyard - not an aerial and not an elevation. The pool runs across the foreground with loungers and palms on a landscaped deck, and the residential wings rise on the left, right and far side with their dark timber-slatted balcony screens and pale stone piers. BEST AVAILABLE EXTERIOR - flagged: this is a partial exterior (courtyard/pool deck, three facades seen obliquely, no street frontage and no full building massing). 2560x1385.

LOOKED: EXTERIOR, photograph, ground-level symmetrical view down the same central courtyard - not an aerial, not a render, not a street elevation. A green lawn fills the foreground with flowerbeds and white outdoor seating at the edges; two parallel residential wings frame the shot and a third linking block closes the far end, all showing the dark slatted balconies over beige facades. This is the widest and most complete view of the building Ellington publishes. BEST AVAILABLE EXTERIOR - flagged: still partial, because it is an inward courtyard view and never shows the building from the public road. 2560x1385.
